geometry_edits.rationale: Shift the cantilever slightly earlier to reinforce the dominant gesture while preserving the continuous bar.
Reduce the overhang modestly so the mass reads as a cleaner anchored bar with a more controlled public threshold.
Convert the split-wing condition into a more explicit access-side notch, better matching neighborhood living and the verified frontage.
Place the notch on the access-aligned side in the program frame.
Tune the notch width to create a legible ground opening without breaking the primary mass.
Keep the opening low enough to read as an entry/public seam rather than a full fracture.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the public void into a clearer court rather than a shallow cave, so the ground response becomes legible and programmatic.
Increase the carved court margin to make the void more spatially meaningful.
Align the public opening to the verified access side in the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant bar with a secondary carved-and-split condition, and it is legible across all four views. It does not collapse into unrelated fragments or a view-dependent trick, so the basic massing structure is sound. The parcel response is acceptable but not especially strong: the mass sits within the boundary and the long axis is plausible, yet the open-space figure remains modest and somewhat generic rather than clearly organizing the site. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly; there is some undercut/split evidence, but the ground response does not become a fully convincing public threshold or courtyard aligned to access. Programmatically, the form can plausibly support neighborhood living/mixed use because it keeps a clear primary mass and an active-ish carved condition, but the section is still too boxy and the cantilever/split logic feels more formal than spatially programmatic. The form is coherent enough to pass, but it would benefit from a more explicit carved void or access-side opening and a slightly more articulated section to strengthen public ground and upper hierarchy.
